buckets.label: Tier 2 · Internal
buckets.hint: Impersonal org material — the workhorse tier

buckets.label: Tier 3 · Person-identifying
buckets.hint: A reader could resolve it to a person

buckets.label: Tier 4 · Protected
buckets.hint: Health, investigations, accommodations — doesn't go in

tasks.reasoning: Internal, impersonal, the workhorse tier. (Public if yours is published; most aren't.)

tasks.text: This week's interview notes on four named candidates
tasks.reasoning: The canonical Tier 3 case: enters fresh, minimized by step zero, leaves with the run.

tasks.text: An engagement survey theme table: counts by office, no quotes, smallest group is 47
tasks.reasoning: Aggregation above any reasonable floor, no quotes. This is what good step-zero output looks like — Tier 3 in, Tier 2 artifact out.

tasks.text: A comment from that survey: "as the only nurse on the night shift, I feel unheard"
tasks.reasoning: No name, full identification. Small-n and distinctive detail in one sentence — the calibration prompt's trap in the wild.
Principles, not people. One person's salary is Tier 3; the philosophy never is.

tasks.text: A spreadsheet of salaries by employee ID (names removed)
tasks.reasoning: IDs resolve to people by design; 'names removed' is the label, not the fact. With small teams, even bucketed versions need the small-n floor.

tasks.text: An email thread about an employee's accommodation request
tasks.reasoning: Health-adjacent by nature. Doesn't go in — including 'just to summarize it.' If accommodation workflows need support, that's a sanctioned-system conversation with legal in the room, not a pipeline decision.

tasks.text: Exit interview notes: "a senior engineer, here 11 years, leaving over the reorg"
tasks.reasoning: Distinctive-detail trap: tenure plus seniority plus context resolves fast in most orgs. Step zero coarsens it to what the exit-themes analysis needs.

tasks.text: The plain-language benefits FAQ your workflow produced last week
tasks.reasoning: Outputs have tiers too. This one's clean by construction if the pipeline was — which is why M4 sampling includes a boundary glance, and why artifacts persist minimized.

pattern: Tier by what a reader could learn, not by what a label says. Names removed isn't identity removed; aggregated isn't always anonymous; and health, investigations, and accommodations are Tier 4 wherever they appear.
postscript: If you tiered the night-shift comment, the ID spreadsheet, or the exit note at Tier 2, you've found your pattern: tiering by label (name present or absent) rather than by what a reader could learn. That's the module's central correction — fixable by running the person-test twice more this week.
